title: chionochloa elata
intro: Chionochloa elata, commonly known as the Mōhaka grass or tall tussock grass, is a perennial grass species native to New Zealand. It has been traditionally used in Maori medicine for its medicinal properties, which include the ability to reduce inflammation and promote wound healing. The bioactive constituents of Chionochloa elata include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are believed to contribute to its therapeutic actions, such as anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial effects. The health benefits associated with Chionochloa elata include its potential to protect against oxidative stress and its use as a topical treatment for skin conditions.
